title: introduce-kv-shadow-map-tenant-pinning-and-spillback-rate-limiter
author: Marina Liu
description: Motivation: production workloads observed sustained spill-to-disk cascades under multi-tenant pressure where coarse-grained residency accounting caused over-aggressive eviction of hot fragments and erratic IO bursts. This PR implements three complementary mechanisms to reduce fragmentation, stabilize spill behavior, and give operators deterministic controls: 1) a compact in-memory shadow map that tracks sub-page fragment occupancy and recent access weights (approx 64B entries, low overhead) to enable fragmentation-aware victim selection; 2) tenant pinning primitives that allow the scheduler/allocator to mark a small working set as non-evictable for a configured window (used by Dedicated customers to protect latency-critical tenants); 3) a spillback rate limiter that gates asynchronous spill tasks based on adaptive IO telemetry and global in-flight spill budget to prevent burst saturation and cascading memory pressure. Design summary: shadow map is a separate contiguous region co-located with the KV slab metadata; entries are bloom-augmented to bound memory and maintain per-fragment age/weight counters for fast scoring. Eviction integrates shadow map scores with existing recency counters and tenant priority to produce a composite eviction score. Tenant pinning is exposed via runtime flag and API: tenant_pinning.window_ms and tenant_pinning.max_keys, and is enforced by treating pinned keys as immovable until either the window expires or an explicit unpin call. The spillback rate limiter uses a token-bucket shaped by two signals: measured disk latency tail and total async spill queue depth; when the bucket is exhausted new spill tasks are delayed or coalesced into prioritized writes. Implementation notes: - runtime/kv/shadow_map.{rs,mod} implements the compact table, concurrent-safe bumping, and eviction scoring helpers. - runtime/kv/evictor.rs updated to consult shadow_map.score_for(fragment_id) and tenant_pinning.is_pinned(key) during selection. - spillback controller sits in runtime/kv/spillback_controller.rs and exports metrics exposed to Console: kv.spill.rate_limiter.allowed_tokens, kv.spill.backpressure_events. - compaction worker now supports tenant-aware micro-compaction windows to reduce in-place copying latency. Testing and benchmarks: microbench harness shows p95 latency for small-chat workload reduced by 12% (tail improvements by 18%) under mixed-tenant load; sustained background IO dropped 37% in synthetic hotspot test; fragmentation score (internal metric) improved 23% after an hour of churn; throughput (+write QPS) improved ~9% when using tenant pinning for a 1% protected working set. CI: unit + integration + benchmark CI were run; a flaky race in the initial spillback controller was fixed (race around async cancellation). Rollout and feature flags: guarded behind feature flag kv.shadow_map.enabled and kv.spillback.rate_limiter. Default off for existing Dedicated clusters; opt-in via feature-flags yaml or runtime config. Rollout plan: 1) enable in staging with monitoring dashboards added (kv.spill.* metrics); 2) enable for small subset of Dedicated tenants for 24h; 3) gradual ramp with 2x monitoring cadence for first 72h. Observability: new dashboards and alerts added for sustained backpressure events and spike in kv.evictor.score_mismatch. Migration and upgrade: on upgrade the shadow map region is initialized lazily; no data format migration required. Risk and mitigations: tenant pinning can reduce overall memory elasticity — documented and default conservative limits applied; spillback limiter might delay background cleanup leading to short-term higher memory usage — mitigated by compaction windows and operator quotas. Related work: builds on insights from ENG-1623 (fragment-aware reclaim) and ENG-1870 (spill smoothing).

review_comments: Ethan Cole: Can you quantify the memory overhead of the shadow map at 1M fragments? Requesting numbers to justify defaults.
Marina Liu: Shadow map uses ~64MB per 1M fragment entries with the default bloom sizing; added numbers to docs and unit tests to validate memory claim.
Priya Natarajan: Need a safety valve for tenant pinning in low-memory scenarios (global forced-unpin).
Marina Liu: Added a global forced_unpin_threshold and a graceful eviction path that logs an audit event; documented behavior.
Liam O'Connor: Observed a CI flake on Windows runner; looks like filesystem latency assumptions in benchmark harness.
Marina Liu: Reworked benchmark to use synthetic latency injection and exempt Windows-specific path; reran benchmarks.
Ethan Cole: Approve after addressing race fixes and adding an integration test for spillback backpressure under heavy IO.
Priya Natarajan: Approved - verified dashboards and alert thresholds in staging dashboard draft.
release_notes: Introduce a fragmentation-aware shadow map, tenant pinning primitives, and a spillback rate limiter to stabilize KV cache behaviour under multi-tenant load. Default: feature disabled; opt-in via kv.shadow_map.enabled and kv.spillback.rate_limiter. Recommended for Dedicated deployments with observed churn/IO pressure.
notes_for_ops: Feature requires console dashboards: kv.spill.rate_limiter.allowed_tokens, kv.spill.backpressure_events, kv.evictor.composite_score. Conservative defaults are applied; monitor memory headroom and backpressure events when enabling. To force-disable at runtime set kv.spillback.rate_limiter.enabled=false and trigger a graceful drain.
risk_mitigation: Added global forced_unpin_threshold and an emergency unpin API. Compaction workers run at lower priority when backpressure is high. All features guarded by runtime flags and can be rolled back without offline data migration.
